newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD delay irritates buyer candidates - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD delay irritates buyer candidates - paper.

text.p: The leader of one of the consortia planning to bid in the privatization auction of Brazilian mining giant CVRD expressed displeasure over the delay in the sell-off, the O Globo newspaper reported on Monday.
A 45-percent voting stake in CVRD was due to be sold off April 29, but a flood of lawsuits against Latin America's biggest privatization has managed to suspend the auction until now.

"It is a very unpleasant situation," O Globo quoted Antonio Ermirio de Moraes, chief executive of Brazil's largest private conglomerate Votorantim which leads the Valecom consortium, as saying. "Whether Valecom wins or loses it would be good to reach the end of this soap opera."
He said Brazil was putting on a "third-world show" and without naming those responsible, he said, inability was causing the daily delays of the auction, according to O Globo.

Moraes said the auction delay was causing unnecessary costs, adding that Valecom had already spent $300,000 in the last six months just to determine how much it could bid for the CVRD voting stake, O Globo said.

The government is also losing money over the postponement and is spending 300,000 reais alone on the documentation requested by a judge ruling on the government's "super appeal" against all injunctions issued against the auction, O Globo said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
